name: realme Buds Air8 Pro
_capture_note: OPOv1 (BBK: OnePlus / OPPO / realme). Verified live 2026-09-17 by btsnoop HCI capture of com.realme.link plus static RE of split_realmeHeadset.apk, then confirmed end-to-end by driving the hardware from Orchestra itself. Phone: Pixel 8 Pro (Android 17). Headphone: realme Buds Air8 Pro (MAC 28:04:c6:db:b6:9a, Manufacturer 688 = 0x02b0). Control channel: RFCOMM/SPP to the OPO UUID, DLCI 25. Frame: AA | LEN u16LE (=total-2) | FLAG | cmdId u16LE | transferId u8 | dataLen u16LE | payload; no checksum. cmdId = (opcode << 8) | feature, written little-endian; a reply is cmdId | 0x8000 with the transferId echoed. Full protocol notes in docs/opov1-protocol.md.

protocol._doc: Commands carry the LOGICAL u16 command id (e.g. 0404 = opcode 0x04 SET, feature 0x04 noise control); the opo_v1 codec writes it little-endian. Opcodes seen: 0x01 GET, 0x02 NOTIFY (device-initiated), 0x04 SET, 0x05 REGISTER, with 0x81/0x84/0x85 the matching responses. No hello/register handshake is required before a SET on RFCOMM - verified by setting the mode cold from Orchestra and getting an 0x8404 ack plus a real mode change on the hardware.

functions.title: Noise control

set._doc: Payload is NoiseReductionInfo{deviceAction, type, value} (3 bytes, see tl/protocol/commands/NoiseReductionInfo.java). deviceAction=01, type=01, value=mode. The device acks 0x8404 with payload 00 and then pushes 0x0204 '03 01 01 <mode>'. Mode values are NOT the 01/02/04 given in the public OnePlus write-up - those are wrong for this device.

functions._read_note: The current mode is PUSHed by the device via 0x0204 (topic 0x03), never polled - the vendor app never issues a GET for feature 0x04. GET 0x0104 returns a constant (00 00 00 01) and 0x0109 does not track the mode, so neither is a usable read. Push-based state is not wired up yet, so this function ships without a read block and relies on the optimistic UI. Do not add a read block until a listener is implemented.
